The test image shows a soybean leaf with numerous small, circular spots scattered across the surface. The spots have brown/reddish-brown centers with slightly darker borders. This pattern suggests a fungal leaf spot disease. Top candidates: Frogeye_leaf_spot, Septoria_brown_spot, Cercospora, Phyllosticta_leaf_spot.

Now I'll view one reference from each top candidate class.
The Cercospora reference (107) shows dense, small reddish-purple spots on a yellowing leaf - closer but more dense than the test. Let me continue with other classes.
I need one more class to reach 16 different classes. Let me view Phytophthora and a closer Frogeye reference.

The Frogeye leaf spot reference (103) is a near-perfect match to the test image: hand-held green soybean leaf with small circular spots scattered across the surface, each with a reddish-brown/purple border. The spot size, distribution, and leaf condition are essentially identical.

**Summary of findings:**
- Test image: green soybean leaf, ~25 small circular brown spots with darker borders, no yellowing, spotted uniformly across the leaf
- Frogeye_leaf_spot (103): identical presentation — hand-held green leaf, circular spots with reddish-purple borders, same density and distribution
- Other leaf spot diseases don't match: Septoria has yellowing + dense dark spots, Cercospora has denser smaller spots with yellowing, Phyllosticta has larger irregular lesions, Bacterial_Blight has angular water-soaked lesions
- Root/stem diseases (Phytophthora, Brown_Stem_Rot, White_Mold, etc.) are clearly not relevant
